cards.front: Why must pyruvate be converted before it can enter the Krebs cycle?
cards.back: Pyruvate has three carbons, but the cycle accepts only a two-carbon unit, so the **link reaction** converts it into acetyl coenzyme A first.
cards.hint: Compare the number of carbons in pyruvate with what the next stage accepts.

cards.front: What happens to an acetyl group when it enters the Krebs cycle?
cards.back: It joins **oxaloacetate**, a four-carbon molecule, to form citrate (six carbons). Coenzyme A is released to collect another acetyl group, and citrate is converted back to oxaloacetate so the cycle can repeat.

cards.front: Where is most of the energy from the link reaction and Krebs cycle held?
cards.back: In the **reduced carriers** (reduced NAD and reduced FAD). They carry hydrogen to the final stage, where most ATP is made; only a little ATP forms directly in the cycle.
cards.hint: Think about what the carriers do next.

cards.back: The removal of a carboxyl group from a molecule as **carbon dioxide**.
The removal of hydrogen atoms from a molecule, usually passing them to a carrier such as NAD.
cards.hint: Think of what is lost from the molecule, not gained.

cards.front: Where does the carbon dioxide released in the link reaction come from?
cards.back: From **carbon atoms in glucose**, not from the oxygen gas breathed in. It diffuses out of the cell and leaves the body in the breath.
cards.hint: Trace the carbon back through glycolysis.

cards.front: How many carbon dioxide molecules are released by the link reaction and Krebs cycle when 4 glucose molecules are broken down?
cards.back: **24** molecules. Each glucose gives 6 (2 from the link reaction and 4 from the Krebs cycle), so $4\times6=24$.
cards.hint: Work out the total for one glucose molecule first.

cards.front: How many reduced NAD molecules are formed per glucose molecule across the link reaction and Krebs cycle?
cards.back: **8** molecules: 2 from the link reaction and 6 from the Krebs cycle, which turns twice per glucose.
cards.hint: Add the totals for each stage separately.

cards.front: What are the products of one turn of the Krebs cycle?
cards.back: **2** carbon dioxide, **3** reduced NAD, **1** reduced FAD and **1** ATP.
cards.hint: One turn means one acetyl group has entered the cycle.

cards.front: Why is one turn of the Krebs cycle not the same as one glucose molecule when counting products?
cards.back: One glucose gives two pyruvate molecules, so two acetyl groups enter the cycle. One glucose therefore means **two turns**, so double the one-turn totals.
cards.hint: Count how many acetyl groups each glucose molecule supplies.

cards.back: A **two-carbon acetyl group** attached to coenzyme A, which delivers the group to the Krebs cycle.
cards.hint: Look at the product of the link reaction.

cards.front: How is ATP made directly in the Krebs cycle?
cards.back: By **substrate-level phosphorylation**, where a phosphate group passes directly from a substrate molecule to ADP, giving one ATP per turn.
cards.hint: Compare this with where most ATP is made later.

cards.back: A second carrier molecule, like NAD, that has accepted hydrogen and carries it from the Krebs cycle to the electron transport chain.
